sentences.english: The grandmother loves her own grandson.
The grandson gives a flower to the grandmother.
The grandmother sees a black bird.
The grandson hears the black bird.
And so the grandmother praises her own grandson.
The gladiator carries a heavy shield and a long spear.
sentences.latin: Gladiātor scūtum grave et hastam longam portat.

sentences.english: Many men see the brave gladiator in the city.
sentences.latin: Multī hominēs gladiātōrem fortem in urbe vident.

sentences.english: The brave gladiator gives a clear signal to his own friends.
sentences.latin: Gladiātor fortis suīs amīcīs signum clārum dat.

sentences.english: The fierce enemy is captured in the serious battle.
sentences.latin: Hostis ferōx in proeliō gravī capitur.

sentences.english: And so the men of the city give a great victory to the brave gladiator.
sentences.latin: Itaque hominēs urbis magnam victōriam gladiātōrī fortī dant.

sentences.english: My sister sees the white moon and the many stars of the black night.
sentences.latin: Soror mea lūnam candidam et multās stellās nigrae noctis videt.

sentences.english: The long shadows of the tall forests are made by the bright moon.
sentences.latin: Umbrae longae altārum silvārum ā lūnā clārā faciuntur.

sentences.english: For my sister seeks the truth of the immortal stars in her own mind.
sentences.latin: Nam soror mea vēritātem stellārum immortālium in animō suō quaerit.

sentences.english: The white dawn is prepared by the bright sun after the long night.
sentences.latin: Aurōra candida ā sōle clārō post longam noctem parātur.

sentences.english: And so my sister praises the new dawn and the bright sun.
sentences.latin: Itaque soror mea aurōram novam et sōlem clārum laudat.
